correctness.rationale: For each ordered supported edge q identifies opposite orientations; its kernel is exactly backtrack cycles, generated by explicit admissible Γ-square boundaries (u,v,u,u). Any valid Γ-square maps to ∂[a,b,d]−∂[a,c,d], where both triangles are supported by radius-one-ball conditions. Every simplicial triangular boundary lifts from square (a,b,a,c). Thus q induces an isomorphism of degree-one chain quotients compatible with degree-zero boundary, naturally for hypergraph vertex maps. Explicit Smith reductions and all integer lattice comparisons on seven cases agree. A separately constructed six-vertex closed RP2 triangulation has H1=Z/2. General finite presentations yield all finitely generated abelian H1 groups; no higher homology is claimed.

originality.rationale: The 2026 primary paper defines Γ-homology but supplies only selected first-degree computations and does not state natural agreement with homology of its associated simplicial complex, integrally or with arbitrary hyperedges. The 2016 source treats embedded homology, distinct from Γ in the motivating paper. The 2018/2019 graph comparison treats a different cube (□), already different for the triangle graph. Projective-plane simplicial torsion itself is previously known, while its universal transfer to Γ and the first-homology structural theorem are the new contributions. Full-text investigation of the relevant 2026 and 2016 sources, semantic comparison of accessible claims and targeted published-finding corpus searches did not reveal a dominating result. Residual risk remains.

value.rationale: Theorem computes first integral Γ homology for every finite hypergraph (including nonuniform) by finite simplicial boundary matrices, filling a conceptual gap in a theory just introduced with only isolated examples. It detects arbitrary abelian torsion, yields naturality and a universal realization consequence, and rigorously distinguishes Γ from embedded/□ constructions. These are structurally motivated rather than routine arithmetic observations.
